facts.fact: 店里冷清，她注意到有人进进出出楼上的公寓——看房客衣着整洁；Cynthia 已在办开放式看房。
facts.anchor: It was a slow evening at the shop, so I noticed when couples started going in and out of the apartment above Combat. They looked pulled together, employed. The women peered into the shop windows and their men eyed the street around them.

facts.fact: 她听见看房男女谈价：七大道月租七百太贵、六十七街新厨房离父母近；Cynthia 眼下是出租。
facts.anchor: He was the only man on Seventh Street in slacks. “I dunno, Marcy, seven hundred bucks is a hell of a lot for the place, don’t you think?” So Cynthia was renting for now. Good. “The apartment on Sixty-seventh had a brand-new kitchen, and it’s closer to my parents.”

facts.fact: 回家撞见 Patrick 瘫在门口——他睁眼、摇头说「Oh, fuck me. 你一定是在耍我。」
facts.anchor: Then he opened his eyes, at first only a flutter, and then wide, and then shut them. He shook his head. “Oh, fuck me. You must be fucking joking.”

facts.fact: 她想扶他却扶不住：能碰到手臂却毫无握感，身体无法相接；他（与她同时）意识到他已经死了。
facts.anchor: He tried to stand and I tried to help him, but I couldn’t. I could touch his arm, but I felt nothing in my grip. Our bodies couldn’t connect. “This isn’t real,” he said, just as I was realizing what happened. I opened the door and told him to lean on me, but of course there was no weight to put on my shoulder.

facts.fact: 他说大概是海洛因吸多了；那种止不住的可怕咯咯笑。
facts.anchor: Patrick had a terrible giggle, the kind you can’t shake when something serious happens. “Well. I suppose I had too much heroin.”

facts.fact: 他已无实体也无内在，只剩情绪像天气变化：他说「我在天鹅绒天堂」，闭眼像仍在享受「什么都没有」的奢侈。
facts.anchor: He was all emotion, changing like the weather. His eyes softened. “I was in velvet heaven.” He closed his eyes, and it looked like he was there right now, feeling the luxury of nothing.

facts.fact: 他叙述此前 OD 的经验（醒前很美、醒来像被卡车撞）；这次「我不是在死，我只是在家」；随后「我在沙发上，却站在自己上方看着自己」——他看起来不好。
facts.anchor: I’ve been losing track of time. I didn’t even know I was coming here, but…”

facts.fact: 他把床单蒙在头上问「你能看见我吗」，笑后又有点害怕地再问一遍。
facts.anchor: Patrick somehow pulled the sheet over his head. “Can you see me?” He laughed, but then he said it again, a little scared. “Can you see me?”

facts.fact: 她发现鬼会呼吸（习惯了/喜欢这感觉），而她的注意让他的呼吸变得吃力——他必须提醒自己去呼吸。
facts.anchor: He was breathing. It hadn’t occurred to me that ghosts might breathe because they were used to it, or because they liked the feeling and wanted to keep on. But the minute I noticed it, his breath started getting labored, like he was realizing he had to do it, he had to remind himself, because otherwise nothing in his body would tell him to do it.

facts.fact: 他哭着说：「Mark 不在这儿。」她问：你是来找他的吗？
facts.anchor: “No.” We sat with that for a moment. “Are you here looking for him?”

facts.fact: 那天正是十月二十一日——Mark 本该三十岁；她忆起 Mark 曾对抱怨变老变丑的 François 说「丑男人老了反而好看」。
facts.anchor: It was. It was October 21. He should have been thirty.

facts.fact: Patrick 二十六岁；她想二十六比二十九更糟（还没那么可爱了，而变老又遥远）；二十九岁「准备好结束些什么——但不是生命，不是生命」。
facts.anchor: I asked Patrick how old he was, and he said, twenty-six. I thought about being twenty-six and thought it was a worse age to go than twenty-nine. Twenty-six, you’re starting to feel not so cute. But being older feels so far away. Twenty-nine, you’re ready for something to be over, I thought, being a twenty-nine-year-old myself, but not life, not life.

facts.fact: 他们斗嘴；他做了个「说得也有道理」的表情。
facts.anchor: He made a little face that said “fair enough.”

facts.fact: 她说「也因为是你把他从我这带走」；他答「你是在囤积他」。
facts.anchor: “You were hoarding him.”

facts.fact: 关于「你一个 dyke 居然跟男人上床」，她答「也许我是有双性经验的女同性恋」；两人一起大笑——「老朋友互相说真话」。
facts.anchor: His laugh crackled in the air. Suddenly we were both laughing, old friends telling each other the truth.

facts.fact: 他的脸一变：同时是死人、热辣青年与极度恐惧的孩子，全部孤独——像树被砍倒时的年轮。
facts.anchor: Then his face changed. All at once, he was a dead man, a hot young stud, and a very scared child, all lonely, like rings of a tree when you cut it down.

facts.fact: Patrick：「他曾是我的全部。没有他就没有我。这就是我死的原因。」
facts.anchor: “He was everything to me,” Patrick said. “There is no me without him. That’s why I died.”

facts.fact: 他指出：她以为能把 Mark 变成家人；真正让她暴怒的是 Mark 与他在她进不去的层面上相通；恨他比恨 Mark 容易。
facts.anchor: “You thought you could make Mark your family. It infuriates you that Mark and I could relate to each other on a level you couldn’t. It’s easier to be angry with me than it is to be angry with him.”

facts.fact: 她自陈：Mark 曾是她最好的朋友、她的 bashert；他们注定相遇、注定同行。
facts.anchor: Mark was—had been—my very best friend, my bashert. We were meant to meet and meant to continue on together.

facts.fact: 关于时间：她说本该有更多；他答你有过十年；她说不算够；他说那是你生命的三分之一；她说总有一天会远不到三分之一。
facts.anchor: “And one day it will be much less.”

facts.fact: Patrick 道歉：他真心为她的失去难过。
facts.anchor: He said, “I’m sorry. I am. I’m sorry for your loss, too.”

facts.fact: Patrick 转述 Mark 的圣人岛幻想：全团搬去希腊，Renata 与他在洞穴屋两头各拥情人，大家都在同一锅。
facts.anchor: “One summer I want to live in Santorini. The whole cast picks up and moves to Greece, like when the Brady Bunch went to Hawaii except no one has bad luck. Renata and François and Leon and Paul and all the Davids. Julie wouldn’t give up work for a whole summer, but she’d blow through for a long weekend with some good drugs. Cris would get her heart broken by some local girl and Greg would ruin someone’s life and it would turn out David Green could speak perfect Greek and he’d order for us at the taverna every night. Renata would have her lovers and I’d have mine at the other end of our cave house and we’d all be in the mix together. Is it sad that my island fantasy has my whole regular life in it? But why would I fantasize about paradise and not bring all my friends?”

facts.fact: 她想：在天堂里，他仍想和所有人在一起，包括她。
facts.anchor: If that’s what my selfish heart needed to hear, there it was. In paradise, he still wanted to be with all of us—with me.

facts.fact: Patrick 离开时灯光变了：窗外那盏坏了一整个夏天的街灯闪了闪，亮了。
facts.anchor: And then the light changed. Suddenly, I could make out the shapes in the room, and I couldn’t see Patrick there. The streetlight outside the window was flickering, and then came on. It had been broken all summer.
